title: DAI Adds Depth, Loses Confidence
text: One day brought $17.15M of DAI against $11.71M for the whole trailing week, and its DEX pools gained 11.4% TVL while the liquidity score slid 73 to 62. A $25M single-day print turns drift into rotation.
extended:
DAI added $17.15M in a single day against $11.71M for the entire trailing week, so yesterday supplied the week and then some. The pools tell a less flattering version: DAI's DEX liquidity composite slid from 73 to 62 while pool TVL climbed 11.4% to $233.73M, a depth move that on its own accounts for roughly half a point upward.

A pool that gains $23.85M of depth and sheds eleven points of score is not describing a drain; it is describing coverage marked mixed and a component measuring something other than dollars. DAI holds an A- at 80, sitting inside the 14 A-tier coins that carry 82.4% of mapped supply. This is a confidence question, not a solvency one.

USDC shed $337.35M over seven days to $73.54B, still 8% under its April peak of $79.75B. USDe pulled in $58.25M net with pressure intensity pinned at 100, while Ethereum ran $36.75M negative on the day and the Bank Run Gauge sat at -26.1, CAUTIOUS. Total supply of $318.24B is 0.25% below the Digest-window high set three days ago.

apxUSD widened from 301 to 359 bps at $0.964, day 77 of the STRC drawdown that first took it to $0.89 in June. GUSD closed a 108-hour, 201 bps excursion. DEWS cut ALERTs from 12 to eight but printed a WARNING in GGBR at 57. PSI held 91.5 on its seventieth BEDROCK day. Clear $25M of DAI in one session and the drift becomes rotation.

title: USDS Yield Reading Arrives Without Receipts
text: USDS tops the risk board at 5.68% APY with no evidence to back it, and five yield flags outshouted a shrinking depeg field. USDC added billions, mcap moved +0.15%, and 13 of last week's calls missed.
extended:
The top of this week's risk board is not a depeg but USDS flashing a yield warning: 5.68% APY against a 7d average of 5.59% and a 30d of 6.01%, on a $6.70B book, tagged opportunity-evidence-missing. PSI slid from 92.6 to 91.2, its worst reading landing Aug 30, yet the band never left BEDROCK. The largest severity score of the week, 6729.1, came from a coin nobody is positioned to fear.

USDS was one of five NEW THIS WEEK yield flags: USD1 spiked to 2.06% APY against a 30d of 1.01%, USDe read 4.27%, PYUSD sagged to 4.82% on tvl-outflow, and XAUT printed 8.8% while its benchmark degraded. USDS itself repeated the same 5.5-to-5.7% reading four straight days from Aug 25 to Aug 28 with corroboration never arriving. The through-line across those five names was yields drifting while nothing else moved.

The depeg field, by contrast, was entirely inherited: pmUSD held 4663 bps below peg on $50.16M, the week's only critical, but it carried over from before Monday. cNGN cratered 9993 bps yet on $2.78M mcap it barely registers. Unique depeg signals fell to 11 from 14, active observations to 121 from 140, and grade transitions held at zero for a second straight week.

USDC was the largest weekly mover all six days, adding $1.91B on Aug 26 and still accelerating $319.98M on Aug 29, yet total mcap crept only +0.15% to $318.79B. The Bank Run Gauge midpoint jumped from 8.9 to 21.9 week over week even as it dipped to -19.3 on Aug 28. Blacklist events exploded to 437 from 85, though the $19.28M frozen barely cleared last week's $16.15M: a locksmith rekeying every door in the building to catch one shoplifter, almost all of it USDT on Tron.

That gauge climb of 13 points against flat supply is the tension carried into next week. The forward scoreboard was unkind: 1 hit, 13 missed, 1 expired, 3 pending, so most of last week's calls landed wrong. Next week decides whether USDS's evidence-missing yield either corroborates above 5.68% or clears its tag, and whether the Bank Run Gauge can hold the 21.9 line.

title: Small Flows, Maxed Signals
text: USD1 took in $4.00M and fxUSD $3.02M while rwaUSDi shed $3.96M, all three pinning intensity at 100 on flows worth a rounding error; if the Bank Run Gauge slips to negative 10, this stops being noise.
extended:
USD1 absorbed $4.00M and fxUSD $3.02M over 24 hours, both pinning their intensity readings at 100 against 30-day baselines, while rwaUSDi ran the other way at negative 100 and shed $3.96M. Three stablecoins maxing out their pressure signals on flows worth a rounding error reads as repositioning, not growth.

PSI holds at 91.2, still BEDROCK on a 68-day streak, yet that is its softest reading in 19 days and breadth crept to 7.36. Twenty depegs stay active: MSUSD widened to 3,765 bps and USDA to 416, both worse than yesterday. The Bank Run Gauge whipsawed from 35.9 to negative 1.5, a 37-point swing back toward neutral.

USDC added $374.09M on the week to $73.98B, the largest mover on the board and the reason today reads as allocation, not alarm; total supply sits at $318.79B, a hair under the Digest-window high set a day ago. Next trigger: if the Bank Run Gauge slides to negative 10 or lower, the fxUSD and USD1 flows stop being noise and flow stress takes the lead.

title: Cash Grows, Yield Empties
text: USDC booked $319.98M of its $518M weekly gain in a single day, nearly the $400M rotation line; USYC shed $101.90M in the same session, dumping most of its weekly bleed at once. Cash in, yield out.
extended:
USDC added $518.48M over seven days to reach $74.19B, the market's largest weekly mover and, by Circle's own history, a trickle: it once minted $6.55B in a single week. The pace is the tell. USDC booked $319.98M of that total in the last 24 hours, meaning most of a slow week landed in one session, just shy of the $400M that marks rotation.

USDT tells the opposite story: +$33.74M in a day against +$1.17B for the week, its growth already spent. The rotation reads cleaner at USYC, which shed $101.90M yesterday, nearly all of its $147.14M weekly drawdown compressed into one session. Money leaves a yield-bearing treasury token for plain cash while PSI holds at 91.7, its 67th straight BEDROCK day.

The Bank Run Gauge clawed back to 35.9 [HEALTHY] from yesterday's -19.3, and apxUSD sits unchanged at 315 bps below peg, day 74 of its STRC-driven drawdown. Next trigger: USDC clearing $400M in a single day turns allocation into rotation, and USYC crossing $130M of one-day outflow would confirm the exit is a decision, not noise.

title: apxUSD Recovers As The Gauge Flips
text: apxUSD tightened to 294 bps from 337 as the Bank Run Gauge flipped +21.2 to -19.3; PYUSD bled $42M, FDUSD $11.9M, 21 depegs still open. One coin healing, the flows turning.
extended:
apxUSD tightened to 294 bps below peg from 337 a day earlier, clawing back from the 3,159 bps crater the STRC drawdown left last June. At $313.59M it is the largest break on the board that isn't pmUSD, and one of the few moving the right way among 21 active depegs. It still trades at $0.970 with an F on backing.

The flow side moved the other way. The Bank Run Gauge flipped from +21.2 to -19.3 [CAUTIOUS] in a single session, with PYUSD shedding $42.07M and FDUSD $11.88M against their 30-day baselines; only AUSD leaned positive at +$6.28M. PSI held at 91.7 [BEDROCK], its lowest since August 11 but a 66th straight day in the band. pmUSD sits unchanged at 4,648 bps under.

DEWS pushed its ALERT count to 10 from 8, AUDm crossing up from WATCH even as most of the board drifted calmer, a split screen that rarely resolves quietly. The next tell is the gauge: if it falls to -25 or lower, flow stress graduates from footnote to headline. AUSD's lone positive pull is the one number arguing against that.

title: USDS Sheds A Week In A Day
text: USDS lost $287M in one session, almost its entire weekly decline, while its yield slid under the 30-day average. USDC added $1.46B the same week. Another $360M day turns drift into rotation.
extended:
USDS shed $287.44M in a single session, roughly three-quarters of its $375.58M weekly decline compressed into one day, and the outflow is accelerating. It lands on a token carrying an A- safety score and a 5.65% yield that has drifted below its 30-day average of 6.04%. Capital is leaving the paying door here, not a broken one.

The backdrop stays placid: PSI holds at 92.1, a 65th consecutive BEDROCK day, with depeg severity at 0.03. USDC added $1.46B on the week even as USDS drains, the largest issuer expanding while a smaller peer contracts. Mint and burn echoed the tilt, USDG down $31.65M and AUSD down $9.20M over 24 hours, though the Bank Run Gauge held at a healthy 21.2.

PMUSD widened again to 4,663 bps below peg at $0.534, an ongoing critical that has stopped surprising anyone. The number that decides tomorrow is USDS: another $360M single-day exit reclassifies this from drift to rotation, and with $287M already gone, that threshold is one ordinary session away.

title: The Rotation Into Yield
text: USDY drew $24.99M in net mints at max intensity; stUSDS and U joined the pressure while USDC bled $96.61M on the day. Yield is winning the allocation.
extended: USDY pulled in $24.99M of net mints over 24 hours, pinning its pressure gauge at 100 against a 30-day baseline; stUSDS added $10.77M and U another $9.98M at the same maximum intensity. Three yield-bearing tokens hitting peak inflow pressure on the same day is not a coincidence, it is a preference. The money came from somewhere. USDC reversed to minus $96.61M on the day even as it held its $1.91B weekly lead, and BUIDL accelerated $142.80M in a single session. PSI reads 91.8, a 64-day BEDROCK streak, while the Bank Run Gauge sagged from 55.4 to 39.6 yet stayed HEALTHY. This is rotation, not flight. USDY's fresh supply arrived while its DEX depth thinned to $13.81M, a token adding coins faster than it adds an exit. PMUSD, still critical, narrowed to 4419 bps below peg on a $52.52M cap. Next trigger: a $125M single-day USDC move turns this drift out of plain dollars into confirmed rotation.

title: PYUSD Erases A Week Overnight
text: $111.63M left PYUSD in a day, erasing a week of gains as APY slid from ~8% to 3.82%. Mint/burn confirms -$97.61M out; the wider market still reads 92.6 BEDROCK.
extended:
PYUSD shed $111.63M in a single day, wiping out the $24.78M it had added over the prior week and then some. The mint/burn ledger agrees: net -$97.61M over 24 hours at maximum burn intensity, two independent pipelines pointing the same direction. The yield tells the rest; PYUSD's APY has fallen to 3.82% against a 30-day average near 8%, and money left the moment the rate did.

PSI holds at 92.6, a 63rd straight day of BEDROCK, a reading that says the system at large feels none of this. USDC embodies that calm, adding $1.79B over seven days to $73.76B, the largest weekly mover on the board. apxUSD, unresolved since June's STRC drawdown, narrowed to 317 bps below peg from 430. The stress is real but still local.

The Bank Run Gauge sits at 55.4 and CONFIDENT with no flight-to-quality flag, which is why this reads as one issuer's problem rather than the market's. Next trigger: if PYUSD sheds at least $140M in a single day, the story graduates from drift to rotation. Should the gauge instead break to -10 or lower, flow stress replaces PYUSD as the thing to fear.

title: USDC's Gauge Climbs As TVL Drains
text: USDC's DEX liquidity score jumped 65 to 78 as $1.23B of TVL left the building. Circle added $1.67B, then stalled to $52.42M. USDS drained to $13.72M. PSI napped at 92.8.
extended: USDC's DEX liquidity score climbed from 65 to 78 this week, the loudest item on the board, even as the TVL behind it drained from $5.40B to $4.17B. That is a fuel gauge reading full while the tank loses more than a billion dollars. PSI never noticed, holding the BEDROCK band all seven days between 91.8 and 94.1 and closing at 92.8, a hair off the 92.5 open. Circle spent the week feeding USDC, adding $1.67B over seven days before the tap narrowed to $52.42M in the final one. USDC ran as the largest weekly mover on four separate days, from +$765.61M on the 21st to the +$1.67B peak by the 24th. The yield desk kept flagging the same two names, USDT at 4.22% APY and USDC at 9.83%, both stamped opportunity-evidence-missing, which is the analytics way of saying the number arrived without a receipt. While USDC's figures puffed up, USDS liquidity collapsed: TVL fell from $162.28M to $13.72M and its score slid 59 to 49 on the 21st before clawing back +10 the next day. DAI went the other way, lifting its score +9 then +8 to 56, and USD1 gained +9 as its TVL nearly doubled from $51.80M to $89.83M. The chronic pmUSD depeg stayed broken at 4433 bps on $52.32M, unmoved and unresolved. Aggregate market cap added 0.48% to $318.06B, a rounding error dressed as growth. The louder week-over-week move was the Bank Run Gauge midpoint swinging from -5.4 to 12.0, even after bottoming at -17.7 on the 22nd. Freezing cooled sharply: 82 blacklist events worth $15.14M this week against 106 events and $51.53M last, most of it USDT on Tron in a single $4.59M action on the 22nd. The forward-look scoreboard closed 13 hit, 7 missed, one still pending, and the misses were mostly bets that USDC's supply surge would keep its liquidity honest. Next week decides whether $4.17B is the USDC TVL floor or the first step down; watch the score-versus-TVL gap if Circle's minting stays near this week's $52.42M crawl rather than its $1.67B sprint.

title: USDC Adds A Billion, Then Stalls
text: Circle added $1.67B to USDC in seven days, then just $52.42M in the last one; USDe burned $21M net and the run gauge slid to -3.8, even with PSI parked at 92.8.
extended:
Circle added $1.67B to USDC across seven days and just $52.42M in the last one, roughly a fifth of the daily pace it kept all week. At $73.65B the largest weekly mover now sits 8% below its April peak of $79.75B, and the drop-off reads less like a pause than a balance sheet finding its level after a strong run.

The flow side tilted the other way. USDe burned a net $21.02M over 24 hours against its 30-day baseline, and the Bank Run Gauge slid from 25.6 to -3.8, neutral but no longer buoyant. DEWS moved eleven names from CALM into WATCH, lifting that count to 99, with satUSD and MAI still parked at ALERT. PSI holds 92.8 BEDROCK on a 62-day streak, total cap 0.20% under its record.

pmUSD holds its ongoing critical break at 4424 bps below peg, unchanged on a $52.39M cap; apxUSD trades 430 bps under after its STRC drawdown, and USDA widened to 242 bps overnight. Next trigger: if USDC's seven-day move clears $2B at the next snapshot, the deceleration was a pause, not a top. Watch USD1's mint pace, running $10.21M a day and accelerating, for the next rotation.

title: Tether Turns On A Dime
text: USDT added $977M in a day, dwarfing its $143M weekly net and reversing yesterday's outflows. USDC still leads the week at +$1.67B; PSI holds BEDROCK at 91.8 for a 61st day.
extended:
USDT added $977M in a single day, a figure that dwarfs its $143M net for the entire week and reverses the outflows that led yesterday's tape. The gap between one day and seven is the whole story: Tether shrank for most of the week, then bought itself back hard. Its A+ card shows backing at 74.7 and exit liquidity pinned at 100.

USDC remains the week's largest mover at +$1.67B, lifting it to $73.63B though still 8% under its April high. PSI reads 91.8, its 61st consecutive day in BEDROCK, and it has not slipped below that line since August 11. Severity is a trivial 0.03; breadth barely registers at 6.6, VNXAU and EURS the only names troubling the score.

The peg board stays ugly at the edges: pmUSD widened again to 4433 bps below par, an F-rated $52M holdout still marked at $0.557. apxUSD sits 420 bps under after June's STRC drawdown, its $309M the largest exposure among the broken names. Next trigger: if USDT clears $1B in one day tomorrow, this drift graduates into rotation.

title: Tether Sheds Two Billion
text: USDT burned a net $2.00B in 24h while USDC minted $838.53M; Flight-to-Quality never tripped, so call it rotation. A second $2B day with no offset would call it something else.
extended:
Tether burned a net $2.00 billion in twenty-four hours, an intensity reading pinned at -100, while USDC minted $838.53 million and PYUSD added $100 million the same day. Ethereum carried the drain at -$1.14 billion net. The Bank Run Gauge sits at -17.7, CAUTIOUS, yet Flight-to-Quality never tripped: capital rotated tiers rather than fled them.

That exit left no mark on the aggregate. Total stablecoin cap holds at $318.28B, 0.13% under its Digest-window high set thirty days ago, and PSI reads 92, BEDROCK, its sixtieth consecutive day in that band. Severity is 0.04, breadth 7.68; the largest issuer can shed $2B and the index does not blink.

USDT's supply decline is accelerating, -$863M over one day against -$842M across seven, and 36 Tron blacklist events froze $9.95M in the window. pmUSD widened again to 4,351 bps below peg at $0.565, its 2,695th hour underwater. If USDC keeps minting into Tether's burn next session, this stays rotation; a second $2B USDT day with no offset reads as exit.

title: USDS Pool Empties, Score Shrugs
text: USDS bled 91% of its DEX liquidity to $13.72M in a day; a $6.71B coin now backs its on-chain exit with pocket change, and the composite score fell only ten points.
extended: USDS lost 91% of its DEX liquidity in a day, its pooled TVL draining from $162.28M to $13.72M while the composite score slipped a mild-looking ten points, from 59 to 49. That score understates the wound: a $6.71B stablecoin now backs its on-chain exit with $13.72M of depth, nearly 500 to 1 against the float. USDS's advertised yield is fading too, 5.59% APY against a 30-day average of 6.24%, reason for depth to leave rather than deepen. The mirror ran the other way at USD1, whose pool nearly doubled to $89.83M and lifted its score from 57 to 66; USDY thinned alongside USDS, its score sliding to 28. PSI reads 93 and BEDROCK, off from 94.1, a 59-day streak the index shrugs through even as DEWS ALERT names tripled from three to nine overnight. pmUSD remains 4,241 bps below peg, wider again. Next trigger: if USDS's liquidity score falls to 41, the drain has follow-through rather than a one-day flush.

title: Scores Rise, Pools Thin
text: Four DEX liquidity scores rose; only DAI's pool actually grew. USDC's jumped 13 to 78 while its DEX TVL fell $1.23B to $4.17B, and USD0 and FDUSD gained on thinner pools.
extended:
DAI's DEX liquidity score climbed nine points to 56 on $8.75M of added pool depth, the only honest liquidity gain of the day. Three larger names improved on shrinking pools: USDC's score jumped thirteen to 78 as its DEX TVL fell $1.23B to $4.17B, while USD0 gained fifteen and FDUSD fifteen more, both on thinner pools. The model is applauding what the pools are quietly withdrawing.

PSI held its BEDROCK footing at 94.1, a 58-day streak, while total supply crept to $317.15B, still 0.48% under its window high. USTB led the week with a $697M mint, triple its prior single-week record, and USDC added $507M in a day. pmUSD widened marginally to 4,001 bps below peg at $0.600, no change in its 2,647-hour trajectory.

apxUSD's slow repair continues from its June STRC drawdown, 521 bps off peg against a 3,159 bps low, the rare depeg number moving the right way. USDC's yield already cooled to 9.83% from an 11.07% monthly average, exactly as flagged. The next tell is whether USDC's liquidity score reaches 86 while TVL keeps falling; if it does, the score is grading reputation, not exit depth.

title: USDC Sheds, USDe Absorbs
text: USDC lost $359.6M on the week while USDe pulled in $107M, $56M of it yesterday alone; a thinning 10% reward is loosening the incumbent's grip on its float.
extended:
USDC shed $359.6M over the week, the largest single move on the board, and with it went the assumption that its float is sticky. The money did not evaporate: USDe absorbed $107M across seven days, $56M of it yesterday alone, nearly all of it routed through Ethereum's $88.9M net inflow. At $71.87B, USDC now sits 10% below its April peak.

The headline market barely registered the move: $316.21B total, up a rounding-error $52.93M on the week and 0.78% under the Digest-window high set 27 days ago. PSI holds at 92.9, its 57th straight BEDROCK day. The rotation reads cleaner beside the yield tape: USDC's best APY cooled to 10.07% from a 30-day 11.15%, and a thinning reward loosens a float.

The depeg board stayed ugly but familiar: apxUSD widened to 668 bps on its documented STRC drawdown, while pmUSD ground on at 3878 bps below peg, unchanged enough to pass for furniture. USDC's APY has already slipped under its 11.7% cooling line; if it breaks the 9.76% seven-day average next session, the $360M reads as exodus, not rotation.

title: USDT Grows Without Paying Up
text: USDT pulled in $964M this week at a flat 4.12% yield; USDC, paying 9.26%, lost $376M. The name offering double the reward is the one bleeding float.
extended:
USDT's best advertised yield sits at 4.12%, dead flat against its 7-day average, and the issuer still pulled in $964M of fresh supply this week to reach $182.95B. USDC, paying 9.26%, shed $376M over the same seven days. The largest name grew without touching its rate; the one dangling more than double the reward is the one that bled float.

The cooling runs across the board: USDC's 9.26% is down from an 11.51% 30-day average, USDS eased to 5.75% from 6.35%, and each flagged anomaly kept reverting toward baseline. The Pharos Stability Index reads 92.5, its 56th straight day in BEDROCK, severity a rounding error at 0.03. Nothing here demands attention; the numbers merely invite it.

pmUSD remains 4003 bps below peg, 54 wider on the day and no closer to resolution after 108 days. DEWS keeps 8 names at ALERT, MAI and pmUSD leading on cross-source divergence. The lone yield still climbing is USD1, spiking to 3.27% from a 7-day average near zero; whether it holds above its 1.41% 30-day baseline next session decides if the print was signal or noise.

title: USDT's Yield Reading Won't Hold Still
text: USDT's top risk flag this week was a data gap, not a depeg: yield printed 0.51%, then 8.29%, then 4.12% on $183B unmoved. Nine names hit DEWS ALERT while PSI shrugged at 92.2.
extended:
The week's top risk flag was not a break but a blank: USDT's 08-15 yield warning pinned 4.12% APY against a $183.05B market cap and stamped it opportunity-evidence-missing, an alert on the largest stablecoin that the analytics could not corroborate. PSI opened at 91.1 on 08-11 and closed at 92.2, never leaving BEDROCK, so USDT's marquee event was a telemetry shrug rather than a wobble.

USDT ran through every column this week. Its yield feed read 0.51% APY on 08-11 and 8.29% by 08-12 before settling near 4.12% for four straight days, the analytics equivalent of a thermometer that cannot decide between hypothermia and fever. Supply lurched alongside it: down $1.24B on 08-11, a $1.01B reversal on 08-12. And Tron did the rest, with 106 blacklist events freezing $51.53M, more than double the prior week's $24.52M despite 83 fewer actions, led by a single $32.56M seizure on 08-12.

The counter-story was resolution. USDA cleared its 802 bps break after 869 hours, and XAUm closed 918 bps in 23 hours; only pmUSD held on, 3949 bps below peg at $57.41M mcap. The quieter concern lived in DEWS, where nine names sat in ALERT by 08-17 as RLUSD, XAUT, TUSD and USX all shed liquidity in one session, and the Bank Run Gauge sank to -12.6.

Capital barely moved in aggregate: mcap rose 0.34% to $316.41B on the week yet landed flat at -0.06% versus last week. XAUT was the largest mover at +$2.67B even as its liquidity score fell 64 to 56, while USDC added $832.43M on 08-12 then bled $437.61M by 08-17. USDe's liquidity slid 59 to 50 as TVL dropped $85.37M to $58.72M.

Twenty of twenty-one daily triggers resolved as hits, with one pending and zero misses. With nine names in ALERT and the gauge at -12.6 heading in, the next trigger is whether DEWS converts to the first grade transition after zero recorded this week.

title: Nine Names In ALERT
text: DEWS ALERTs climbed from six to nine as RLUSD, XAUT, TUSD and USX all shed liquidity in one session. PSI's 92.2 registers none of it; the Bank Run Gauge, sinking to -12.6, does.
extended:
Nine stablecoins now register DEWS ALERT, up from six yesterday, and the liquidity scores feeding that band are sliding together. RLUSD dropped 63 to 54, XAUT 64 to 56, TUSD 50 to 32, USX 57 to 47. Four exit doors narrowing in a single session is a pattern, not an accident, and the warning band widened to match.

The Pharos Stability Index reads 92.2, a 55-day BEDROCK streak indifferent to any of it. The Bank Run Gauge disagrees, sagging from -6.0 to -12.6 and back into CAUTIOUS territory. Five sessions ago RLUSD was where money went; yesterday $15M of mints reversed and walked out the door it arrived through.

pmUSD remains the open wound at 3949 basis points below peg, wider again with no resolution. apxUSD, still bleeding from June's STRC drawdown, sits 619 bps under. Yield is the one number cooperating: USDC's best rate eased to 9.52%, USDT to 4.12%. If DEWS ALERTs cross ten next session while liquidity keeps sliding, the gap between 92.2 and the periphery stops being academic.

title: USDf's Score Outruns Its Cash
text: USDf's liquidity score jumped 11 to 58 while $1.9M left its pools; satUSD's fell with its TVL, down 72% to $732K. The grade rewards how depth sits, not how much shows up.
extended:
USDf's DEX liquidity score climbed eleven points to 58, the kind of move that usually signals money arriving. It didn't: TVL fell from $25.02M to $23.16M over the same window. The score reads depth and concentration, not dollars parked, so a $1.34B stablecoin posts a healthier grade while its pools quietly thin.

satUSD offers the honest version: its score cratered from 34 to 14 as TVL collapsed 72% to $732K, both metrics agreeing for once, on a $158.7M float. Four of five liquidity movers diverged from their own TVL today, proof the grade rewards how depth is arranged, not how much shows up. PSI holds at 93.1, its 54th straight BEDROCK day, indifferent to small-cap exit doors.

pmUSD widened again to 3,880 bps below peg, 106 days underwater and still without a floor. A liquidity score that rises while liquidity leaves is either a tribute to concentration or a coin grading its own homework. Next session's tell: whether USDf's 58 holds as TVL keeps draining, or whether the grade reconverges with the $23M actually parked there.

title: apxUSD Widens, Fifty-Nine Days In
text: apxUSD slid another 206bps to 713 below peg, now $0.928; on a $300M float it edges even pmUSD for the board's largest depeg impact. The STRC drawdown that opened it in June still hasn't closed.
extended:
apxUSD slid another 206 basis points off peg today, from 507 to 713; it now trades at $0.928. On a $300.97M float, that hands it the single largest depeg impact on the board, edging even pmUSD, which sits far deeper. The cause hasn't changed since June 2: the STRC drawdown that first cracked it to $0.89. Fifty-nine days on, its report card still reads F, backing 39.5.

PSI eased to 92.7 from 94.6, its lowest in three days, though a 53-day BEDROCK streak makes that a rounding error, not a warning. Dollar yields kept compressing: USDT's best APY held at 4.12%, USDC's slipped to 10.16% against 11.42% a month back. pmUSD, 3,501 basis points below peg at $0.650, did nothing new.

title: USDC's Reward Wears Thin

title: Stress Picks Its Names
text: DEWS doubled its WARNING tier to two and drained WATCH from 99 to 91 names; apxUSD tripped ALERT while UTY holds 57 on $21M. PSI slipped to 92.1, its lowest in 16 days.

text: 13.38% APY on $73.28B, well past an 8% base, and the source that pays it never shows. USDT cooled to 5.59%, USD1 sank to 0.96%; the yield tape reads noisy, not rich.

title: BUIDL Blinks, USDS Drains Daily
text: BUIDL flipped CALM to WATCH on supply velocity while USDS shed over $900M a day for five sessions. PSI held BEDROCK at 94.6 before closing at an eight-day low. A scheduled redemption, not a run.
extended:

The counter-move was broad de-escalation: USDT added $1.20B on July 15, grade transitions fell to 10 from 29, and blacklist dollars collapsed to $13.48M from $67.36M the prior week. Standing conditions held their posts: apxUSD stuck at 3159 bps on a shrinking $297M, pmUSD at 5568 bps, and USX pinned near $0.39 well past its 600th hour, chronic depegs the aggregate has priced in. The Bank Run Gauge widened from -11.9 to 29, midpoint up to 11.4 from 6.7, and USDT again flashed a 7.73% best yield with no evidence behind it.

The forward-look board closed 4 hit, 5 missed, 7 pending; the misses outnumbered the hits, and the syrupUSDT names that shed 26% of TVL were not the ones we flagged. Next week decides whether USDS's daily $900M redemption finds a floor or whether BUIDL's WATCH hardens into the ALERT the $528M DEWS ceiling already touched.

text: pmUSD held the leaderboard at 5,568 bps while USX, apxUSD, and USDA joined critical severity by 07-13. PSI climbed 91 to 93.4 in BEDROCK; mcap slipped 0.26% to $336.66B.
